items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The Huston's were from way down South and their son came to Cincinnati to live with them... He and I worked at this fruit sugar-coating factory

ctx.x: persuaded them to spend their summer vacation in Lexington, Ky., his home town, and play the summer dance season in Kentucky. The original leader of the band was Horace Henderson, a pianist, but he was not with the band then, because Edgar Hayes was also a pianist and a hell of a good one. Some of the musicians in the band at that time were Joe and Casper McCord and Henry Hicks. Joe and Cass played saxophones and Hicks played trombone; but the strong man of the band was Freddie Jenkins, the trumpet player I had…

Dad, my brother and I moved from 9th Street to Hathaway Street and I went to work in a fruit sugar-coating factory. There was a family living on the first floor by the name of Haddins that were distant cousins of ours. One of the Haddins had married the daughter of my Aunt Mary. On the second floor was a family named Huston. We had two rooms and a kitchen on the third floor and there was a man that lived in a small room on the side of our front room.

The Huston's were from way down South and their son came to Cincinnati to live with them after we had been living on Hathaway Street a few months. This fellow was older than I and he loved to carry a pistol. He and I worked at this fruit sugar-coating factory which was at least 6 miles from where we lived. We rode the street car to work and walked home when the work day was finished. My sister stayed with us sometimes and with my mother at times.
